translated_text: November 22, 1940. The change, my love, asking for your handwriting. I received good news from your parents. Always the long letter in [illegible]. Your father, your mother, and [illegible] all wrote; they are very well, have enough to eat, and want to come to France for the holidays. But your father is just worried about us; he suspects something. He asks if we are still together and if there are any changes at home. They are asking for your handwriting, Sarah in particular, who sent me the first photo that was taken of you. You were exactly 6 months old and you are exactly the same as you are today. It's lovely. You'll see, it's very cute. I'm going to write them a report and you write it next time, or if you want, I can send you a text. Could you copy it for them? I'm also going to write to Jeanette that we received good news from Prague - I was so, so happy! They wrote the letter on February 5th. This afternoon I'm going to my mother's. Otherwise, everything is fine. Keyshone paid 525 francs. Your little one, don't be too stingy. Change it into bills. You have 3, well, we'll manage for the future. What I was given... Did I already tell you that 2500 francs... 2 places in Tunis?! In the newspaper. What do you want more? [illegible] Write, my darling, today you received a similar letter. I adore you and I want so much already, so much to see you, my darling. - PARIS 69 22 1140 1530 RUE VOUILLE PARIS 69 22 1140 1530 2.GE DE VOUILLE Mr. Robert Zweigenthal Reg 6th comp.. [illegible] SP 2197 AR AUX 27-2 POSTE * MEES
